U0000.meaning: Protective equipment—including personal protective equipment for eyes, face, head, and extremities, protective clothing, respiratory devices, and protective shields and barriers—must be provided, used, and maintained in a sanitary and reliable condition wherever necessary due to hazards of processes or environment, chemical hazards, radiological hazards, or mechanical irritants encountered in a manner capable of causing injury or impairment in the function of any part of the body through absorption, inhalation, or physical contact.

source_spans.quote: (a) Application. claim_judgments.rationale: C0000 reproduces 29 CFR 1910.132(a) faithfully, capturing the general requirement that protective equipment be provided, used, and maintained in a sanitary and reliable condition wherever necessary due to process/environmental, chemical, radiological, or mechanical hazards. All dimensions are properly represented.

C0001 faithfully extracts 29 CFR 1910.132(b), establishing employer responsibility for assuring the adequacy, maintenance, and sanitation of employee-owned equipment when employees provide their own protective equipment.
C0002 faithfully extracts 29 CFR 1910.132(c), requiring all personal protective equipment to be of safe design and construction for the work to be performed.

Paragraph (g) (S0/F023) explicitly governs paragraph (d), stating that paragraph (d) applies only to §§ 1910.133, 1910.135, 1910.136, 1910.138, and 1910.140, and does not apply to §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137. C0003 omits this governing scope limitation from both scope_text and summary, thereby making the workplace hazard assessment duty overbroad by admitting excluded standards (such as respiratory and electrical PPE). Therefore, scope and summary are errors.

C0004 extracts the equipment selection and employee use duty under paragraph (d)(1)(i), but fails to incorporate the governing scope condition of paragraph (g) (S0/F023), which restricts paragraph (d) to specified PPE sections and excludes §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137. This renders scope and summary overbroad.

C0005 extracts the requirement to communicate selection decisions under paragraph (d)(1)(ii), but omits the governing limitation in paragraph (g) (S0/F023), which restricts the scope of paragraph (d) and excludes §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137. Consequently, scope and summary are overbroad.

C0006 extracts the requirement under paragraph (d)(1)(iii) to select PPE that properly fits each affected employee, but omits the governing applicability limitation established in paragraph (g) (S0/F023). Scope and summary are therefore overbroad.
C0007 accurately extracts the non-mandatory advisory statement regarding Appendix B complying with the requirement for a hazard assessment. Modality is correctly identified as not_stated.

C0008 captures paragraph (d)(2)'s written certification elements for hazard assessment verification, but fails to include the governing scope constraint from paragraph (g) (S0/F023), making the requirement overbroad across excluded standard sections. Scope and summary are errors.
C0009 faithfully captures paragraph (e), prohibiting the use of defective or damaged personal protective equipment. Modality is correctly identified as must_not.

C0010 extracts the employer training duty from paragraph (f)(1), but omits the governing scope limitation from paragraph (g) (S0/F023), which specifies that paragraph (f) applies only to §§ 1910.133, 1910.135, 1910.136, 1910.138, and 1910.140, and not to §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137. Scope and summary are overbroad.
C0011 details the required employee training subjects from paragraph (f)(1)(i)-(v), but omits the governing limitation in paragraph (g) (S0/F023). Scope and summary are overbroad.

C0012 extracts paragraph (f)(2), requiring employees to demonstrate understanding and skill prior to performing work requiring PPE, but omits the governing applicability limitation from paragraph (g) (S0/F023). Scope and summary are overbroad.

C0013 captures the retraining mandate and all three specified trigger conditions from paragraph (f)(3), but fails to include the governing limitation of paragraph (g) (S0/F023), which excludes §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137. Scope and summary are overbroad.
C0014 faithfully captures paragraph (g), identifying the precise sections to which paragraphs (d) and (f) apply and do not apply. Modality is correctly identified as not_stated.

C0015 accurately states the general mandate in paragraph (h)(1) that PPE used to comply with part 1910 be provided at no cost to employees, along with its explicit exception clause referring to (h)(2) through (h)(6).

C0016 faithfully extracts the payment exemption in paragraph (h)(2) for non-specialty safety-toe footwear and prescription safety eyewear provided off-site wear is permitted. Modality is correctly not_required.
C0017 faithfully extracts paragraph (h)(3) regarding metatarsal guard footwear reimbursement exemptions when metatarsal guards are provided and employee-requested shoes/boots are used.
C0018 faithfully extracts paragraph (h)(4)(i), establishing that the employer is not required to pay for logging boots required by 29 CFR 1910.266(d)(1)(v).
C0019 faithfully extracts paragraph (h)(4)(ii), providing that the employer is not required to pay for everyday clothing.
C0020 faithfully extracts paragraph (h)(4)(iii), exempting employers from paying for ordinary weather protection clothing and skin creams.
C0021 accurately captures paragraph (h)(5), requiring the employer to pay for replacement PPE except where the employee has lost or intentionally damaged it.
C0022 accurately extracts the first sentence of paragraph (h)(6), permitting employer allowance of employee-owned adequate PPE without mandatory reimbursement.
C0023 accurately extracts the second sentence of paragraph (h)(6), prohibiting employers from requiring an employee to provide or pay for PPE unless specifically excepted.
C0024 accurately captures paragraph (h)(7) regarding the effective date of February 13, 2008 and the implementation deadline of May 15, 2008.
C0025 accurately conveys the Note to § 1910.132(h), stating that specific payment provisions in another OSHA standard prevail.
